summary.text: Maritza Davila is the incumbent Democratic nominee for NY State Assembly District 53 and is unopposed on the November ballot. A longtime Bushwick and Williamsburg community organizer who worked with the Ridgewood Bushwick Senior Citizens Council, she has served in the Assembly since 2013 and chairs its Committee on Social Services. According to her official biography, she focuses on tenant rights, affordable housing and support for low- and middle-income families.

paragraphs.text: Maritza Davila was born in Catano, Puerto Rico, and moved to Bushwick, Brooklyn, as a young girl; she has lived there since and raised three children there as a single mother.
Wikipedia gives her birth year as 1963.
She earned an associate's degree (AA) in Political Science from Long Island University in 2013.

Davila began her public-service career as a community organizer on education, healthcare, public safety, affordable housing, open space and economic-development issues in Bushwick and Williamsburg, and she served on boards and advisory committees including community gardens, local NYPD precinct councils and area hospitals.

She was president of the Community School District 32 board of education and, while directing a statewide lead-paint awareness program, developed a concern for the educational needs of children with disabilities in Bushwick and Williamsburg.

She was a founding member of the North Brooklyn Coalition Against Domestic Violence, serving on its board for two years, and founded the Northern Brooklyn Residents Association, a community advocacy group that supported affordable housing and community development.

In 1996 she joined the Ridgewood Bushwick Senior Citizens Council, where she helped found a local credit union, organized merchant, tenant and block associations, and worked on job training and affordable housing.

Davila won the District 53 Assembly seat in a 2013 special election, with 51.91% of the vote according to Wikipedia, and took office on November 6, 2013, succeeding Vito Lopez; she has been re-elected since.
In 2018 she was appointed chair of the Assembly's Puerto Rican/Hispanic Task Force, and as of January 2023 she chairs the Committee on Social Services while remaining a task force member.
She also sits on the Alcoholism and Drug Abuse, Children and Families, Housing and Rules committees.

According to her official biography, she has worked on relief efforts after Hurricanes Maria and Fiona, COVID-19 vaccination access and food relief in her district, and she hosts an annual Community Holiday Drive with North Brooklyn elected officials and merchants.
